# Better Auth Gotchas

> Known Better Auth framework patterns that cause silent failures or TypeScript errors. Load all HIGH entries before writing any Better Auth integration code.

## Entries

- [Use better-auth/react for React hooks, not better-auth/client](client-import.md): better-auth/client returns framework-agnostic atoms, not callable React hooks. Import from better-auth/react instead. HIGH.
- [verifyEmail token goes in query param, not top-level body](verify-email-token.md): GET endpoints put params in the query object. Passing token at top level causes a TypeScript error and the call fails. HIGH.
- [Cross-subdomain cookies require explicit config](cross-subdomain-cookies.md): Cookies don't travel between subdomains by default. Must enable crossSubDomainCookies with a leading-dot domain. HIGH.
- [Browser auth client uses import.meta.env not process.env](browser-env-vars.md): process.env does not exist in browser or Cloudflare Pages. Use import.meta.env.VITE_* variables. HIGH.
- [Method names are camelCase from URL paths -- check types](method-names.md): Method names are derived by camelCasing the URL path segments. Guessing from docs is unreliable; check the dist type definitions. MEDIUM.
- [signIn two-factor response: check twoFactorRedirect, not redirect](two-factor-redirect.md): The twoFactor after-hook replaces the whole response with `{ twoFactorRedirect: true, twoFactorMethods }` -- there is no `redirect` key, but the inferred type still says there is, so checking `data.redirect` type-checks, is always false, and drops every 2FA user into a silent no-op sign-in that middleware bounces back to /login with no error and no code prompt. HIGH.
- [twoFactor.enable requires the user's current password](two-factor-enable-password.md): Calling twoFactor.enable() without arguments throws TS2554. Must pass { password }. MEDIUM.
- [Organization plugin creates separate tables from custom schema](org-plugin-tables.md): BA's organization() plugin auto-creates its own `organization` + `member` tables. Custom `organizations`/`team_members` tables are a separate system -- frontend writes to BA tables, backend checks custom tables, causing silent FORBIDDEN. HIGH.
- [toNodeHandler + reply.raw bypasses Fastify CORS plugin](fastify-cors-bypass.md): Mounting BA in Fastify via toNodeHandler with reply.raw skips the entire plugin chain. @fastify/cors never runs for auth routes. Must add CORS headers manually. HIGH.
- [setActive() requires organization ID, not slug](set-active-org-id.md): Using slug in setActive causes silent session context loss. Always use the UUID id field. HIGH.
- [Organization plugin doesn't model hierarchical tenancy](organization-plugin-no-hierarchy.md): Plugin is single-level only. For broker -> org -> user or workspace -> team -> user, build the upper layer as a parallel partner_memberships table; do not nest orgs or add parent_organization_id. HIGH.
- [Plugin `after` hook handlers must return an object, not undefined](after-hook-must-return-object.md): runAfterHooks reads result.headers/result.response with no null guard, so a void `return;` throws a TypeError AFTER the endpoint succeeded -- turning a 201 into a 500 with side effects already applied. Return `{}` in every path, or wrap the handler in createAuthMiddleware. HIGH.
- [magic-link verify is a GET that signs in -- link scanners consume the token](magic-link-verify-get-scanners.md): `/magic-link/verify` is a GET that atomically consumes the token then sets a session cookie, so Defender Safe Links and every other mail prefetcher signs ITSELF in and the real user's click lands unauthenticated; `allowedAttempts` is explicitly ignored in 1.6.23, so limited-reuse is not a mitigation. Land the emailed link on an inert interstitial and consume via POST -- the shape better-auth already uses for password reset. Magic link also bypasses the twoFactor plugin's matcher entirely. HIGH.

- [better-auth generate (Kysely/pg) introspects a LIVE database](generate-needs-live-db.md): generate connects to the configured DB to diff the schema and fails offline with a SASL/connection error; point it at a reachable Postgres or hand-write the schema from the plugin's schema.mjs. MEDIUM.
- [mcp() plugin: mirror /.well-known to root; getMcpSession ignores expiry](mcp-plugin-oauth.md): [DEPRECATED mcp() plugin -- use @better-auth/oauth-provider for new servers] OAuth endpoints live under /api/auth but MCP clients fetch /.well-known/oauth-* at the domain root, and getMcpSession returns expired tokens as valid -- mirror discovery to root and check accessTokenExpiresAt yourself. HIGH.
- [mcp() plugin deprecated -- use @better-auth/oauth-provider for OAuth 2.1 MCP servers](oauth-provider-mcp.md): The built-in mcp() plugin is deprecated in 1.6.x; use the separate @better-auth/oauth-provider + jwt() plugins. Set allowUnauthenticatedClientRegistration for self-registering MCP connectors; verify tokens with issuer=<origin>/api/auth (not the bare origin); serve RFC 9728 protected-resource metadata yourself (resource scopes only, no openid); pin @better-auth/cli on its own (lagging) range; use organizationHooks.afterCreateOrganization (not organizationCreation.afterCreate). HIGH.
- [Custom consent page must echo the signed oauth_query in the POST body](consent-page-oauth-query.md): A custom @better-auth/oauth-provider consentPage must POST `oauth_query` (its full signed URL query) back to /oauth2/consent, or the endpoint returns 400 invalid_request "missing oauth query" and the whole OAuth flow is blocked. The endpoint reads the request from a before-hook keyed on ctx.body?.oauth_query, not from the page URL. HIGH.
- [oauth-provider resource server rejects every token (opaque tokens + wrong JWKS/issuer)](oauth-provider-resource-verification.md): Connector authorizes but every /mcp call 401s ("integration rejected the credentials"). The provider only mints a JWT when the token request sends an RFC 8707 `resource` (default it via a /oauth2/token before-hook), and oauthProviderResourceClient derives jwksUrl/issuer from the bare baseURL (fetches <origin>/jwks 404, expects issuer <origin> not <origin>/api/auth) -- pin jwksUrl + issuer explicitly. HIGH.
- [oauth-provider MCP discovery fails in strict clients: AS metadata issuer mismatch](oauth-provider-strict-client-discovery.md): protected-resource metadata advertises authorization_servers: [<origin>] but the AS issuer is <origin>/api/auth, so strict RFC 8414 clients (Antigravity/Gemini) report "no authorization server metadata found" and show no sign-in button. Advertise <origin>/api/auth and mirror metadata at the path-inserted well-known. HIGH.
- [oauth-provider dynamic client registration returns 200 instead of 201 through Next.js](oauth-provider-dcr-201-status.md): The register handler sets 201 but toNextJsHandler downgrades it to 200 on the wire; strict clients reject DCR with "registration failed with status 200". Intercept POST /oauth2/register and normalize a successful response to 201. HIGH.
- [oauth-provider refresh breaks silent re-auth with RFC 8707 resource binding](oauth-provider-refresh-resource-binding.md): Strict clients (Antigravity) omit `resource` on refresh-token grants, so the provider mints an opaque audience-less token the resource server 401s -- auth silently drops every hour and the client masks it as re-login. Default `resource` via a /oauth2/token before-hook and accept the default audience; offline_access must be in granted scopes for a refresh token to exist at all. HIGH.
- [MCP connectors never request custom OAuth scopes -- tiered scope designs are silently bypassed](connectors-never-request-custom-scopes.md): AI connectors only request openid profile email offline_access, so custom read/write/admin tiers are never granted; either tokens satisfy no tools or the server widens defaults and read-only authorization becomes fiction. Surface the tier choice on the consent screen and bind it to the grant. HIGH.
- [trustedProviders does NOT bypass requireLocalEmailVerified when linking a social login](account-linking-requires-local-email-verified.md): Pre-provisioned users created with emailVerified=false hit account_not_linked on their FIRST Google/Microsoft sign-in; trustedProviders only waives the incoming provider's email check, not the local user's. Set requireLocalEmailVerified:false (safe only with closed signup) and/or provision users verified. HIGH.
- [sendVerificationEmail inside emailAndPassword is silently ignored](email-verification-config-placement.md): The verification-email sender only works in the top-level emailVerification block; nested in emailAndPassword it is ignored with no error and no email ever sends. Keep sendOnSignUp off when invite flows mark mailboxes verified themselves; trigger auth.api.sendVerificationEmail explicitly. HIGH.
- [Minor better-auth upgrades silently add REQUIRED plugin columns (2FA lockout)](plugin-schema-drift-on-upgrade.md): A version bump added failedVerificationCount + lockedUntil to the twoFactor table; the hand-maintained Drizzle schema lacked them, so the adapter threw "field does not exist" and 500'd /two-factor/enable for every new enrollment (pre-upgrade rows masked it). Diff the plugin's schema.mjs on every upgrade; migrate AND redeploy the schema. HIGH.
- [Server-side auth.api.* calls silently drop Set-Cookie](server-api-drops-set-cookie.md): `auth.api.signUpEmail` (and every session-minting endpoint) writes the session cookie into better-auth's INTERNAL response headers; a direct `auth.api.*` call returns only the parsed body and discards them. Passing `req.headers` is an INPUT and does not plumb the response back out. The user, membership, and session rows are all created correctly so nothing errors -- the response just has no Set-Cookie, and the new account lands signed out ("logged in as a generic user with no permissions", then logged out on refresh). Use `returnHeaders: true` and forward `headers.getSetCookie()` on EVERY return path, or register `nextCookies()` last (bigger blast radius). HIGH.
- [Behind a two-hop proxy, rate limiting silently collapses into ONE global bucket](rate-limit-shared-bucket-multi-hop-xff.md): `getIPFromHeader` returns null for a multi-hop x-forwarded-for unless trustedProxies is set, so every client shares the key "no-trusted-ip" -- with the magic-link plugin's 5-per-60s rule that is five sign-ins per minute for your entire user base. A 429 on /magic-link/verify never consumes the token, so it presents as `?error=INVALID_TOKEN` with a live token still in the DB, and the only standing symptom is a blank session.ipAddress. Enabled in production only. HIGH.
- [twoFactor() is unusable for step-up when the deployment has no password auth](two-factor-unusable-without-password-auth.md): `twoFactor.enable()` requires the user's current password and offers no other enrolment path, so on a magic-link/social-only tenant nobody has one and EVERY user fails at enrolment -- after the plugin imports, configures, migrates and type-checks cleanly. Worst for step-up auth, which is exactly what a password-less deployment wants. `better-auth` also bundles no passkey plugin, so that pivot does not resolve either; own the credential tables and drive WebAuthn via @simplewebauthn (or hand-roll RFC 6238). HIGH.
- [`__Host-` cookies require useSecureCookies:false, which is not the downgrade it looks like](host-cookie-prefix.md): better-auth exports `HOST_COOKIE_PREFIX` but never uses it, and `useSecureCookies` does not gate the `Secure` attribute -- it only picks `__Secure-` vs `""` as a NAME prefix, so it is the only thing blocking `cookiePrefix` from reaching position 0. Leaving it true emits a `__Secure-` cookie any sibling subdomain can shadow with a `Domain=`-scoped cookie of the same name (session fixation; forced OAuth `state`/PKCE), and every test still passes. Set `useSecureCookies:false` + `cookiePrefix:"__Host-app"` and keep `secure` in `defaultCookieAttributes`; the OAuth `state` cookie inherits it from the same getter. Pin the emitted name in a test -- nothing else fails when someone "fixes" the flag. HIGH.
- [Social sign-in promotes emailVerified in the DB but the session it mints keeps the old value](social-signin-emailverified-stale-session.md): `handleOAuthUserInfo` promotes an existing `emailVerified:false` row with `await updateUser(...)` and discards the return value, so the session is built from the pre-update object -- the row says 1 and `getSession()` says false, and any gate reading the session refuses the user on the very sign-in that verified them. Self-clearing on the next sign-in, so it reproduces once per account and looks flaky; secondary storage caches the stale object and makes it outlive the request. Triggered the first time you synthesise `emailVerified` in `mapProfileToUser` (Entra `xms_edov`, genericOAuth), which makes the fix look like it never deployed. Re-read the row before refusing, and match the integer form SQLite/D1 returns. HIGH.
- [better-auth 1.7 ships no CLI -- generate with getMigrations(), diff with getAuthTables()](cli-gone-generate-programmatically.md): `better-auth generate` cannot run on 1.7 (no bin; @better-auth/cli stops at 1.5.0-beta.13), so a hand-written SQL schema drifts on every bump and Better Auth 500s on INSERT in production -- one 1.6->1.7 bump caused three separate outages, the last latent until key rotation. Generate via getMigrations() into a NEW numbered migration; gate CI with getAuthTables(), which is pure and needs no database. HIGH.
